questions.q: Which of the following is the state animal of Bihar?
questions.explanation: According to the gazette issued by the Government of Bihar on 7 May, 2013, the state animal of Bihar is the Bull (Bos taurus), the state bird is the Sparrow (Passer domesticus), the state tree is the Peepal (Ficus religiosa), and the state flower is the Marigold (Tagetes spp.).

questions.q: In which year, the Nalanda University was re-established in Bihar?
questions.explanation: After the Nalanda University Act, 2010 was passed by Parliament, the university actually began its academic session in September, 2014 with the enrollment of the first batch of students. This is considered the year of its re-establishment.

questions.q: Where is the 'Gullak Bachcha Bank'?

questions.explanation: ‘Gullak Bachcha Bank’ is a collective bank for poor children, located in Patna. Accounts are opened in this bank for children aged 8 years to 16 years. Here, a child’s account can be opened for just `10. This bank is operated through the Bihar Government’s Education Department institution ‘Kilkari Bihar Bal Bhavan’. The operation of this bank is done by the children themselves.

questions.q: What is the tagline of Bihar State Tourism Development Corporation?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Bihar State Tourism Development Corporation is responsible for the development of tourism in the state. The tagline of the Bihar State Tourism Development Corporation/ Bihar Tourism is ‘Blissful Bihar’.

questions.q: What is the significance of ‘Bihar Day’, which is celebrated every year on 22 March?

options.A: On this day, the State Reorganisation Commission created Bihar
options.B: On this day in 1873 CE, Bihar was taken out of the United Provinces
options.C: To commemorate the separation of Bihar from the Bengal Presidency in 1912
options.D: To celebrate the naming of Bihar by Muslim rulers in the 12th century
options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Bihar Day is celebrated every year on 22 March. It may be noted that on 22 March 1912, the announcement was made to separate the Bihar and Odisha Division from the Bengal Presidency. However, this came into effect on 1 April 1912.

questions.q: Under the Digital Bihar programme, which students will receive computer education and training from 2021-22 onwards?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Under the ‘Digital Bihar Programme’, students of all classes from Class VI onwards will receive computer education and training from the academic year 2021–22.

questions.q: Nearly 55 percent of the total population of Bihar survives in absolute poverty because: I. Bihar lacks in natural resources, both existing and potential. II. Bihar has the fastest total fertility rate in India. III. Bihar has very unfavorable agro-climatic conditions. IV. Bihar lacks in quality infrastructure and businessfriendly environment. Which of these reasons are correct?
questions.explanation: After the division of Bihar, all its natural resources went to the state of Jharkhand, resulting in a lack of natural resources, both existing and potential. In terms of total fertility rate, Bihar is among the states with the highest rates in India. Bihar’s Total Fertility Rate (TFR) is recorded as 3.0 [ NFHS- 5 (2019–21)], whereas NFHS-4 it was 3.4 (2015–16).

questions.q: The 'Operation Prahar' in Bihar is related to

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: To realize the vision of a crime-free Bihar, the Bihar Police started Operation Prahar. Operation Prahar is being conducted in Bihar against persons involved in serious criminal incidents as well as against those who violate the liquor prohibition law.

questions.q: Cow slaughter was banned by a law in Bihar in which year?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Through the Bihar Animal Preservation and Improvement Act, 1955, the slaughter of cow, calf, bull and buffalo (shebuffalo) was prohibited in Bihar.

questions.q: Which of these is true?

options.A: Bihar has been a major producer of coal and mica.
options.B: Bihar was separated from Orissa in the year 1911.
options.C: Bihar borders Odisha after the formation of the state of Jharkhand.

questions.explanation: Bihar was a major producer of coal and mica, but after the formation of Jharkhand state, this is no longer the case. Odisha (Orissa) was separated from Bihar and made a new province in 1936. After the formation of Jharkhand state, Bihar does not share a border with Odisha. Bihar has a bicameral legislature.

questions.q: Which of the following items is not registered as a Geographical Indication (GI) of Bihar?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Assam’s Muga silk was granted the GI tag in 2007, whereas Bhagalpuri Jardalu mango, Katni paddy (Katarni rice) and Magahi paan of Bihar were granted the GI tag in 2018.

questions.q: From the last few years Buddhist monks in Bihar are agitating to have control over–
questions.explanation: In recent years, Buddhist monks have been protesting in Bihar to obtain control over the Mahabodhi Temple at Gaya. For the first time, the Sri Lankan Buddhist monk Anagarika Dharmapala raised this demand in 1891 AD, stating that the Mahabodhi Temple at Gaya should be under the control of Buddhist monks. Nagarjuna Surai Seshai, President of the All India Mahabodhi Temple Liberation Committee, also placed the demand for control of the Mahabodhi Temple by Buddhist monks before the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).

questions.q: Where is the lunatic asylum situated in Bihar?
questions.explanation: At the time of the question, the mental asylum in Bihar was actually located at a place called Kanke in Ranchi, at the Ranchi Institute of Neuro-Psychiatry & Allied Sciences (RINPAS). At present, Ranchi is the capital of Jharkhand.

questions.explanation: Rashmi Kumari of Bihar is a renowned international carrom player. She has been the winner of the 2nd, 3rd, 5th and 6th Asian Carrom Championships, the 1st and 4th Carrom World Cups, the 1st Malaysia Open Carrom Championship (1999), etc.

questions.q: The late actor Kumudlal Ganguly, also known by his stage name Ashok Kumar, was born in which of the following cities of Bihar?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Actor Kumudlal Ganguly (Ashok Kumar) was born on 13 October, 1911 in Bhagalpur, Bihar. He died on 10 December 2001 in Mumbai.

questions.q: Which medal did Ritik Anand of Bihar win for India at the 24th Summer Deaf Badminton Olympics held inBrazil?'

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The 24th Summer Deaflympics were held in Brazil from 1 to 15 May, 2022. Ritik (Hrithik) Anand of Bihar won a gold medal in the badminton team event.

questions.q: Who is the Brand Ambassador of Khadi in Bihar?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In February 2022, the Bihar Government announced Bhojpuri singer and Lok Sabha Member of Parliament (from North- East Delhi) Manoj Tiwari as the Brand ambassador of Khadi in Bihar. In November, 2022, folk singer and currently a Bihar Legislative Assembly member, Maithili Thakur, was made the brand ambassador of Khadi and handicrafts in Bihar.

questions.q: At one time, the Naxalites were limited to only West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh in India. Now they have extended their activities in these states, also.

options.B: Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh
options.C: Madhy Pradesh, Maharashtra, Jammu & Kashmir, Rajasthan

questions.explanation: At the time of the question, the Naxalism-affected area in India had expanded to Odisha (Orissa), Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Maharashtra, Telangana and Bihar. According to updated data, Naxalism in India is now concentrated in Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana. At present, Bihar has become free from Naxalism.

questions.q: Shri Nibaran Chandra Dasgupta belonged to –
questions.explanation: Shri Nivaran Chandra Dasgupta was born in Bikrampur (present-day Bangladesh). He was the Headmaster of the Purulia District School in the then Province of Bihar and Orissa (Purulia is in present-day West Bengal). His place of work was the Purulia district of present-day West Bengal.

questions.q: Manvi Madhu Kashyap recently became Bihar's first transgender
questions.explanation: Manvi Madhu Kashyap became the first trans woman to become a Police Sub-Inspector after qualifying in the Bihar Police Sub-Inspector Competitive Examination, the result of which was declared in July, 2024. Two other transgender candidates were also selected in this examination, but they are trans men.

questions.q: Shreyasi Singh, Member of the Legislative Assembly, who has represented India in shooting in Paris Olympics 2024 was elected from which constituency in Bihar ?
questions.explanation: Shreyasi Singh is a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party in the Bihar Legislative Assembly, elected from the Jamui Assembly constituency in the 2020 and 2025 Assembly elections. She won a gold medal in the women’s double trap shooting event at the Commonwealth Games, 2018 held in Gold Coast.

questions.q: Which community was categorized as Scheduled Caste (SC) by a 2015 Bihar government notification which was quashed in july, 2024 by the Supreme Court, ruling that states cannot make changes to the SC list published under Article 341 of the Constitution ?
questions.explanation: In its 2015 notification, the Bihar Government classified the Tanti-Tantwa community, earlier included in the Extremely Backward Class category, as a Scheduled Caste (SC). This was set aside by the Supreme Court in July, 2015. The Supreme Court held that states do not have the power to modify the SC list published under Article 341 of the Constitution. Under Article 341, the list of Scheduled Castes for the states is issued by the President through a Constitutional Order, and any amendment can be made only by Parliament through legislation.
